residuals: Darwin flock is advisory; same-euid, root, or Full-Disk-Access code can mutate reachable objects. Mutations observed by the joins fail closed, but the design does not provide hostile same-user isolation.

RENAME_EXCL prevents replacement of an already-present final leaf at the publication call but cannot atomically compare-and-rename one exact inode; post-joins detect rather than prevent every transient namespace or ancestor ABA.
Final open does not request O_NONBLOCK. A hostile same-euid FIFO replacement could block before the subsequent type and vnode rejection.

Open, fsync, F_FULLFSYNC, and transition-lock acquisition have no outer deadline. F_FULLFSYNC is the strongest exposed Darwin flush request, not mathematical proof against every device, firmware, power-loss, or filesystem failure.
The owner or store-grant lifetime can expire after the last pre-rename lifetime check; success still proves the frozen ordered checks, not a continuously live external clock authority.
A crash after staging creation or final publication but before receipt leaves an unadopted orphan and cannot become PASS in this slice.
Crash-cut, restart adoption, ENOSPC/EIO/partial-write evidence, authenticity, anti-replay, Merkle commitment, encryption, backup/snapshot exclusion, and secure deletion remain later work.
The production paired boundary is enforced by fileprivate call structure rather than an unforgeable lock-token type; NSLock has no fairness guarantee.

The EPR_H4_PRIVACY_TESTS-only interstice deliberately waits without a timeout while both transition locks are held. Deterministic try-lock probes precede release, but a reentrant callback or failed release orchestration can deadlock the test harness; no callback or probe exists in production.
